title: Some tea or the tea
goal: Mark a particular object with -y, -i, -ny or -ni, and leave a general one bare.

intro.text: A bare object means some or any: *Çaý içýärin* (I drink tea). A particular one takes `-(n)Y`: *Çaýy içýärin* (I'm drinking the tea). After a vowel it is *-ny* or *-ni*: *almany*. Names always take it: *Aýnany görýärin*.

exercises.question: *Men alma alýaryn.* and *Men almany alýaryn.* What is the difference?
options: The first is any apples, the second a particular apple.
The first is now, the second every day.
The first is polite, the second familiar.

why.1: Both are in the same tense. The ending *-ny* makes the object particular: **the** apple.
why.2: Neither is more polite. *almany* is **the** apple, *alma* is apples in general.

exercises.explain: A bare object is general: *alma alýaryn*, I'm buying apples. With *-ny* it is particular: *almany*, the apple.

exercises.text: Men çaý___ içýärin, sen süýt___ içýärsiň.
exercises.en: I'm drinking the tea, you're drinking the milk.

reject.why: The vowel of *çaý* is *a*, a back vowel: *-y*.
*süýt* ends in a consonant, so the ending has no *n*: *süýti*.
The vowel of *süýt* is *ü*, a front vowel: *-i*.

exercises.explain: Both words end in a consonant (*ý* is one): *çaý* + *-y* with a back vowel, *süýt* + *-i* with a front one.
*alma* ends in a vowel, so the ending is *-ny*; its vowel is back like the *a* of *alma*.

reject.why: A name as an object always takes the ending: *Aýnany*.
A name as an object always takes the ending: *Aýnany*.
*Aýna* ends in a vowel, so the ending is *-ny*: *Aýnany*.

exercises.question: Which sentence means **I'm selling the phone**?

why.1: Without the ending it is any phone, or phones in general: **I sell phones**.

exercises.prompt: Are you buying the eggs? (to a friend)

exercises.explain: With *bu* in front the object is particular, so it takes the ending: *surat* (back *a*, ends in a consonant) + *-y*.

reject.why: Without the ending it is water in general: **we drink water**. **The** water takes *-y*: *suwy*.
*suw* ends in a consonant, *w*, so the ending is *-y*: *suwy*.

exercises.question: What does Kerim say?
exercises.explain: *Nahary häzir iýýärin*: I'm eating the meal now. The meal Mähri made is a particular one: *nahary*.
